data.turoyo: Madam məlli "ʕal aʕ ʕayne", lazəm yo m ayko, towe, mfayadnole ḥḏo. Kobaʕno, d obitule i barṯaṯxu.
data.translation: Nachdem ich gesagt habe: Auf die Augen! Muss ich ihm, woher auch immer, eine Frau finden. Ich möchte, daß ihr ihm eure Tochter gebt.

rationale: Thin Infectum 1; recipient suffix and quantified human theme distinguish procurement from marrying.

summary: Active II has a procuring/finding agent, theme and optionally an l-recipient/beneficiary; -lan in the existing handmill example is coreferential with the agent. A woman procured for another person in 113/140 does not establish a marriage sense.
Detransitive Infectum presents availability/findability with a location and suppressed agent, often under negation. Utensils, people/spirits and intellect fit the same pattern.

The permitted pyd lookup confirms identical Kurdish etymology and parallel II forms. kmipayəd at PrS 84/53 belongs provisionally with its p-series, not automatically with fyd because the latter happens to contain a Detransitive box. This run makes no change to the separate pyd entry.
Only source-faithful examples without alignment warnings are selected. The supplied oven quotation has a clean cut but a flagged verse-level pairing, so its German is withheld as required.
JL 18.6/1 and JL 18.6.1 denote the same supplied handmill quotation; 102/25 and 113/69 are also already quoted. No duplicate examples are added.
Should pyd and fyd be kept as dialectal variants with cross-references, or merged by editors? In particular, file kmipayəd (PrS 84/53) under pyd unless independent dialectal evidence supports fyd.

For 94/269, supply the verified verse/translation boundaries: the Turoyo includes the beginning of /270, while the German covers only the oven tools. No translation from that flagged record is quoted.
Do speakers distinguish generic availability from potential findability in these Detransitive clauses, or is the difference entirely contextual?
Abstract ʕaql as a located/findable theme in the brain patterns with persons and objects; no new sense of losing sanity is inferred from the verb alone.
